1.name: Maple Park Pond
1.access: Open to everyone. Kids, retirees, ducks.

fish.note: The neighborhood legend. Kids say he once ate a duck.

2.name: Mullet Canal
2.access: Public banks and bridges. Fish right off the bridge.

fish.note: Florida pays a bounty on these. Lou handles the paperwork and refuses to touch it.
A tarpon the size of a canoe that lives under the Canal Road bridge.

3.name: Pelican Point Lake
3.access: Private. The groundskeeper patrols 6 AM to 7 PM. A golf polo gets you past him by day.

fish.note: A largemouth so big the members call it a water hazard.

4.name: Sunrise Koi Pond
4.access: Security walks the plaza day and night. A lanyard gets you in during business hours, but nobody fishes the koi pond.

fish.note: A giant koi that has outlasted four CEOs.

5.name: Storm Drain
5.access: Needs a flashlight and waders. Pitch dark down there.

fish.note: Four missed calls from MOM.
An alligator older than the storm drain. You let him go. He let you go.

6.name: Power Station Outflow
6.access: Fenced, guarded and on camera, with a floodlight at night. Warm water, mutant fish, crowds of manatees. Bring a Geiger counter.

fish.note: It hums.
The third eye follows you around the room.
The heads disagree about everything, including which way to swim.
Reads 40 on the Geiger counter. Lou keeps it in a coffee can, far from the other coffee can.
It says SAFETY FIRST. Somebody didn't.
A forty-pound eel that glows bright enough to read by. It shows up on the plant's own security cameras.
A glowing goliath grouper. A guy from the university paid cash and asked no questions.

7.name: Low Street (king tide)
7.access: Only during a king tide: every fourth day, 10 AM to 2 PM.

fish.note: Caught between a mailbox and a minivan.

8.name: Manholes
8.access: Anywhere in the street, with a pry bar from Lou's. You never know what's down there.

fish.note: It squeaks. Sadly.
Left foot. There is never a right foot.
Gross.
Somebody at the grocery store is having a terrible day.
Volume 3. Lou says he already owns it.
It was holding the line, not biting it. Respect.
Lou knows a guy.
Engraved: 'FOREVER, BARB.' Lou knows a guy.
Missing since the parade of '98. The mayor would like it back. So would Lou.

9.name: Back Canal
9.access: Public banks along the south side. A mangrove creek connects it to Mullet Canal. Pythons.

fish.note: Florida pays a bounty on these. Lou handles the paperwork and refuses to touch it.

10.name: Sunsplash Lagoon
10.access: Theme park, open 9 AM to 6 PM, $8. Staff sweep the park at closing. Hide in the restroom and the lagoon is yours.

fish.note: Somebody dumped their aquarium.
It has teeth like a person. Lou won't look at it.
It still blinks.
Lives under the fake volcano. The park says it isn't real. The bite marks on the boats say otherwise.
It weighed something different every time you looked at it, and the photo shows only a blur. Lou paid cash and locked the door.

11.name: Heron Lakes Pond
11.access: Gated community. Slip in behind a resident's car, or paddle up the back channel. The HOA president walks the pond 7 AM to 9 PM.

fish.note: The HOA stocks them to eat the weeds. Allegedly.
It's addressed to you. Already.
A grass carp that has chaired every HOA meeting since 1994.

12.name: Airport Drainage Canal
12.access: Fenced. Patrol truck, gate guard, and a tower spotlight at night. When a jet comes over, nobody's watching.

fish.note: Invasive. The state says remove it. Lou says sell it.
Unopened. Still a better meal than the flight.
An alligator gar that lives in the culvert under the runway. Pilots call it the speed bump.

13.name: Downtown River
13.access: Public river walk through downtown, from the airport canal to the bay. Bars, bridges and boat traffic.

fish.note: Somebody's sports car is still parked at the River Room.
It still has the rental QR code. It's still charging somebody.
A snook as long as the bar. It lives under the River Room's dock lights, and the bartenders throw it lime wedges.

14.name: Mullet Bay
14.access: Public: the Municipal Pier, Mullet Beach and the seawall. The marina docks are private after 9 PM. Kayaks stay inside the channel markers.

fish.note: The last photo on the phone still clipped to it is of this exact pier.
Real gold. Lou bites it and loses a filling.
A bonefish so spooky it has never been photographed. Until now.
A goliath grouper that has lived under the marina docks since the marina was a fish camp. Protected. You get a photo and a sore back.

15.name: Offshore
15.access: Deep blue water past the channel markers. Skiff only. Squid, big rods, big fish.

fish.note: Catch and release, and a photo you'll show people for the rest of your life.
Protected. It looks at you like you owe it money.
Property of the National Weather Service. Lou sells it to a kid as a UFO.
A blue marlin with a scar shaped like Florida. Trent Marlowe has chased her for eleven seasons.
An endangered sawfish older than the pier. You let it go, with a photo the size of a billboard.

16.name: Marlowe Tower Pool
16.access: Private plaza downtown. A lobby guard until 10 PM, a patrol and cameras all night. A suit gets you past the patrol in business hours.

fish.note: Somebody wished for something. Now you have their penny.
Engraved: 'TO TRENT, FROM TRENT.' Lou knows a guy.
Ten thousand shares. Worth exactly what Lou paid for it.
Trent Marlowe paid forty thousand dollars for it at an auction in Singapore. It's worth more to you as a story.

17.name: Bayfront Park Fountain
17.access: Public park downtown. Nobody minds. The ibises might.

fish.note: About three dollars in quarters. You feel bad. You keep them.
An albino catfish the mayor released in 1989 'as a symbol of civic renewal.' Nobody has told the mayor.

20.name: Calder Reservoir
20.access: Public: Lakeside Park, the boat ramp and the top of the dam. Kayaks and skiffs welcome. Deep, cold and clear.

fish.note: The fish of ten thousand casts. Lou won't believe this one.
A muskie as long as a canoe that has ruled the reservoir since the dam went in. Locals swear it once ate a mallard on live TV.

21.name: The Spillway
21.access: The tailwater below Ironwater Dam. Fish it from the public pier and the river walk. The boil right under the gates, and the wing walls beside it, are restricted: a ranger by day and cameras all night.

fish.note: Jumps like a tarpon, tastes like a gym sock. The catfish love it.
It grunts. Really. Locals call it a sheepshead.
A flathead catfish older than the dam, living in the boil right under the gates. Divers who inspect the dam won't go near that corner.

22.name: Calder River
22.access: Public river walks on both banks, all the way through town. Fish off the bridges or under the I-90 viaduct, where walleye wait in the lights at night.

fish.note: A fish with a canoe paddle for a nose. Been around since the dinosaurs.
Protected. Older than you, maybe older than your grandfather. Back it goes.
A pale old lake sturgeon that cruises under the I-90 viaduct after dark. Nobody keeps the Ghost.

23.name: The Mill Race
23.access: A stone channel that brings cold reservoir water through the old Halvorsen Woolen Mill. The mill is a condemned demolition site: a foreman by day, a watchman and his dog at night.

fish.note: From the old looms. The mill made blankets for the whole state, once.
A brown trout as fat as a dachshund that's lived under the waterwheel since the mill shut down in 1974.

24.name: Brewery Cooling Pond
24.access: Behind Calder Brewing Co. The carp eat the spent grain and get enormous. Security day and night; a visitor's lanyard gets you in during tour hours, 11 AM to 7 PM.

fish.note: A mirror carp the size of a beer barrel. The brewery put it on a label once. It's been insufferable ever since.

25.name: Riverhawks Splash Pool
25.access: Past the center field wall at Riverhawks Field. A groundskeeper by day and security late at night. Between 5 and 10 PM everyone is watching the game.

fish.note: Signed by somebody. You can't read who.
A largemouth that has eaten eleven home run balls. Probably. The groundskeeper keeps count.

26.name: Founders Park Pond
26.access: A public park pond next to Calder River Outfitters. Ducks, joggers and kids with cane poles. Nobody minds.

fish.note: A carp nobody can remember being small. The plaque on the bench says the park was founded in 1851. Some say the carp was too.

30.name: Inner Harbor
30.access: Public: the Harbor Walk along the seawall, the piers by the subway stations, and the open harbor if you've brought a boat. Stripers and bluefish run here all season.

fish.note: All teeth and bad temper. It bites through cheap line just to make a point.
Good for one ride in 1987.
Still playing something. Faintly.
A striped bass as long as a dinghy that has patrolled the Harbor Walk since the seawall went in. She takes one lure a season, and it's never yours.

31.name: The Narrows
31.access: Public: Narrows Park and its pier. The tide rips through under the Gannet Narrows Bridge, and the big stripers wait in the bridge lights at night. The tower yard by the west tower is restricted: a bridge officer by day and a camera all night.

fish.note: Teeth like a horse, lives in the rocks, fights like it's personal.
A little shark everyone throws back and then complains about.
Protected, and older than the bridge. Back it goes, gently.
Somebody's been paying double for months.
A striper that waits in the shadow of the west tower and takes a cut of everything that swims through the Narrows.

32.name: Fish Market Wharf
32.access: The Gannet Fish Pier. The market runs 3 to 11 AM and the dockmaster runs off anyone who isn't buying; a lanyard passes for a buyer's badge. Afternoons and nights the wharf is quiet and anyone can fish it. Scraps off the cutting tables keep the fish coming.

fish.note: It has legs. Little walking fins. It croaks when you pick it up.
GANNET FISH PIER, stenciled on the side. It smells exactly like you'd think.
A goosefish with a mouth like a mailbox that lives under the cutting tables. The fishmongers feed it heads and swear it knows their names.

33.name: Container Port
33.access: Gannet Marine Terminal. Port police drive the quay around the clock, cameras ride the cranes, and floodlights come on after dark. A lanyard passes for a port pass 7 AM to 7 PM. There's a cut in the fence on Commercial St.

fish.note: Little tunny. Fast as a torpedo, tastes like one too.
The steel lock that holds a container to the ship. One container is now very loose.
Forty pairs' worth, all left feet. There's a box of right ones somewhere off Portugal.
A bluefin tuna that followed a freighter in from the Grand Banks, swam into the berth and never left. The crane operators toss it their lunch.

34.name: The Outfall
34.access: Combined sewer outfall CSO 017, under the Harbor Walk by the pump house. Public, smelly and full of life. Fish it from the walk, upwind if you can.

fish.note: A killifish. It lives happily in water that would kill a goldfish.
A harbor rat. It was holding the line, not biting it. Respect.
Somebody's smiling a lot less this week.
A conger eel as thick as your leg that lives inside the outfall pipe. The water authority divers have a name for it they won't say on the radio.

35.name: Ferry Slip
35.access: Between the two ferry piers at the terminal. Public. The ferry pulls in on the hour and churns the slip, so keep your line clear of it.

fish.note: The best bait thief on the waterfront. It's been eating your worms all morning.
WORLD'S OKAYEST COMMUTER.
A tautog the size of a briefcase that comes in on the 7:15 wake every morning and leaves on the 5:40.

36.name: Rooftop Garden Pond
36.access: Skyline Commons, nine floors up on the Kestrel Ave garage. It's for tenants: the garden attendant waves in anyone in a suit, 8 AM to 8 PM, and security does rounds 10 PM to 6 AM. In between, the elevator's yours.

fish.note: SKYLINE COMMONS · TENANT. Not anymore, it isn't.
A platinum koi worth more than the condo below it. The building's management lists it as an amenity.

37.name: Outer Harbor
37.access: Open water south of the Narrows, past the container port to the harbor mouth. Kayaks are fine inside the channel buoys; past them it's skiff only. Cod, pollock and haddock sit on the deep ledges, and bluefin come in by the mouth.

fish.note: A real bluefin, in the harbor mouth. Your arms will tell this story for a week.
There's a lobster in it. He looks annoyed.
A cod the size of a canoe from the deep ledge at the harbor mouth. The old draggermen say he runs the harbor and takes a cut of every catch.

38.name: Mill Creek
38.access: A tidal creek down the far west side of the city, behind the row houses, from the North End all the way to Union Station. The towpath is public the whole way. It widens into the mill basin at Ferry St, where the old tide mill still turns its wheel, and a kayak can paddle the length of it under the street bridges.

fish.note: A schoolie that came up the creek on the tide and forgot to leave.
From the market on Kestrel Ave. It's been down here long enough to have regulars.
An Atlantic sturgeon older than the tide mill, which is saying something. It noses along the bottom of the basin under the wheel at dawn and dusk. Protected: a photo, and back it goes.

39.name: Public Garden Lagoon
39.access: The lagoon in the Gannet Public Garden on Kestrel Ave, with the footbridge and the swan boats. Public, day and night. The swan boats go round 10 AM to 6 PM, so cast between them.

fish.note: It squeaks. The real ducks are not impressed.
Knocked off a swan boat by a very proud seven-year-old.
A largemouth as old as the swan boats. It lives under the footbridge and has bitten exactly one tourist, who had it coming.

40.name: Kettle Bank Plaza Pool
40.access: The reflecting pool in front of Kettle Bank Tower, between Kestrel Ave and Commercial St. Bank security walks the plaza 7 AM to 8 PM (a suit gets you by 8 to 6), and a camera on the tower sweeps it 8 PM to 7 AM. Mind the sweep.

fish.note: Mostly quarters, and one Canadian dime. Somebody wished for a raise.
Somebody on the 30th floor threw it in after a bad quarter. It's still keeping time.
A goldfish the size of a house cat. The bank had it appraised, twice, and keeps the paperwork in the vault.
